spans.s: utkalita, cf. kaṭakam=utkalitam (IA 14, 30), ‘the camp was pitched’.
utkara (IE 8-5), probably, minor taxes; but see kāru-kara. Cf. upakara, nikara, etc. But see also Ghoshal, H. Rev. Syst., p. 47.
utkarṣa (CII 1), used in the sense of utkṛṣṭa.

utkīrṇa (CII 3), ‘engraved’; a technical expression for the actual engraving of an inscription on copper or stone; sometimes indicated by the word udghāṭita (Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXI, p. 20) and ghaṭita (Ind. Ant., Vol. XII, p. 121). See Ullekhaka, likhita.
utkoṭa (IE 8-5, 8-8; EI 33), Prakrit ukkoḍa; a levy; customary presents to be made on occasions to the king or landlord and others. See Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXIII, p. 56.
ut-kṝ, ‘to engrave’; cf. Prakrit kaṇḍāra, used in some Kannaḍa inscriptions (Bul. Dec. Col. Res. Inst., Vol. XI, 1950, pp. 170-71). Cf. utkīrṇa, udghāṭita, Ullekhaka, Vilekhaka.
utkṛṣṭi (IE 8-8; EI 30), same as Prakrit ukkuṭṭhī (q. v.), Sanskrit utkrośa; wailing.
